title: Gossip Protocol — Scale Without Coordinator in 60s  #systemdesign #coding #ai #software #scortier
description:
28/30

How does a rumor spread through 1,000 people in a college? Same way 1,000 servers find each other.

A thousand servers need to know who's alive. One central coordinator can't handle the load. So how do they keep track?

They gossip. Each node talks to a few random neighbors. Those neighbors talk to their neighbors. Information spreads like a rumor at a party.

Patient zero tells two. Each tells two more. By round 10, the whole room knows. After log N rounds, everyone has it. No central coordinator. No bottleneck.

Here's the trick. Gossip is incredibly resilient. Drop a node, the rumor still spreads. Lose half the network, the survivors converge. Coordination without coordination.

Cassandra uses gossip for cluster membership. Consul uses it for service health. BitTorrent uses it to find peers. Anywhere you need eventual agreement without a leader.

Gossip turns expensive central calls into cheap local chats. Scale becomes free.

Part 28 of a 30-reel system design series.
